reviewed_facts: prepare() preserves Frozen.capture main-thread detachment, deep-copies the request and retains one pending capture; a second prepare is refused.
launch() consumes the prepared capture once and starts the filesystem Thread after OS.create_process has returned a positive pid.
A failed Thread.start drops the consumed capture and thread reference, records _snapshot_error, writes cancellation and retains normal pid/exporting/progress polling until child exit.
Python pack() awaits snapshot_ready and cancellation before target directory/lock/manifest operations, so unpublished capture is not packaged.
The existing _process failure branch sets pid=-1 and exporting=false before emitting one failed completion; it does not clear dirty or adopt a failed save identity.
finish() discards unlaunched prepared references and joins any started Thread; exit discards prepared data and cancels/joins the busy writer.
Legacy start(project,request) remains prepare()+launch(), preserving its previous combined operation contract.
limits: This removes only the HAS snapshot writer filesystem overlap with this process-creation call. Recovery writer/preview threads can remain concurrent; this is not a global CWD serialization fix.
The original Windows launch error and GetLastError were not captured. The original unchanged focused pass and negative churn reproduction are separate observations, not causal proof.
Ownership here means the existing pid-based HasProject lifecycle. No new native retained-handle/incarnation guarantee is established by this patch.

Producer authored32/0 uses real Frozen capture/adoption and Thread with inert persist. Actual app/Storage/packer integration remains for root to execute, including Thread-start failure, immutable snapshot and single false completion.
